claims.statement: The Grupo Julio design defines shipment trailing status as the least advanced associated status and leading status as the most advanced, derived from the containers for the shipment header.
claims.limits: Source explanation only. This is not a mapping to a reviewed SQL aggregation or evidence of any current shipment state.

claims.statement: The design says allocation rules may default from the Item Master, arrive through the shipment interface, or be assigned by a wave step before allocation. claims.statement: The container-creation description first handles allocated shippable units as full containers. It groups remaining non-shippable items by Packing Class and associated container group, using weight, volume and critical dimensions. claims.limits: General behavior described inside an implementation SDD, not a recommendation to omit dimensions or evidence of deployed cartonization. The document proposes a report to identify missing dimensions.

claims.statement: Releasing a wave is described as removing the Wave Not Released hold from generated work so picking becomes eligible, and printing applicable wave documents/labels. Hold codes may also be added or removed through Work Insight.
claims.limits: Documentary distinction between running and releasing a wave. It does not establish effective permissions, printer output or all other holds being removed.

claims.statement: The post-wave cancellation description deallocates the order, deletes created shipping containers and work, and returns the shipment to the pool. Picked items need a separate transfer back to inventory. Shipping work is canceled but replenishment work is not; cancellation fails while related work is actively executed. After release, a warehouse user must cancel because host changes are limited to In Pool.
claims.limits: Historical source contract, not an instruction to cancel operational orders or proof of rollback/atomicity. The SDD separately states that this implementation does not use replenishment.

claims.statement: In the described footwear flow, a picker needs permission to short pick. The permitted path adjusts quantity and selects a short reason; without permission, the user uses Pass to leave the work suspended and contacts a supervisor.
claims.limits: Implementation example. No specific security grant, reason-code set or assessed user behavior is established.

claims.statement: Hanging-item picking uses the EX01 Put to Light integration: picking delivers to a pick-and-drop location, a custom mobile sorting step interacts with PTL, and a PTL confirmation sends information back to SCALE to confirm the next pick and putaway. Folded-item flow is described as similar.
claims.limits: The SDD explicitly defers the full behavior to a separate EX01 document. Hardware protocol, retry/error handling and installed custom code are not supplied by this high-level account.

claims.statement: Shipping Container Insight is described as supporting container type/content changes and unpacking by setting quantity to pack to zero, followed by repacking. The accompanying note requires the container to be in a location whose subclass is Packing before editing its contents.
claims.limits: Documentary prerequisite, not a verified permission or deployed procedure. Closing a container, editing contents and repacking remain distinct actions.

claims.statement: Grupo Julio page 85 says loads can be confirmed when all shipments are Ship Confirm Pending, while its status list on page 48 says Load Confirm Pending (800) means all shipments have been ship confirmed and the load is ready to confirm. claims.limits: The conflicting prerequisite wording is unresolved. Do not choose one as an executable status gate or infer that an upload file has reached the host.

claims.statement: The design distinguishes plan-based counts, which select items/locations and create a separate work unit per selected location, from activity-based requests after warehouse actions such as short picks or crossing a location quantity threshold. It describes reconciliation as confirming on-hand quantity, updating location inventory, recording an inventory transaction and closing the count request.
claims.limits: Frequency examples, threshold screenshots and the existing 9999-versus-zero tolerance conflict are not active deployment settings. No count or reconciliation was executed.

claims.statement: The Labor Management description separates the warehouse action, a generated labor request, processing by a continuously checking Labor Management service, and the resulting detail record used by Labor Activity Insight or a report. Untracked activities may be entered through Manual Labor Entry.
claims.limits: Source-described execution stages, not measured service health, timing or throughput. No request table or service instance is inferred from the prose.

claims.statement: Labor plans select labor groups and their processing sequence for estimated labor during wave execution. The labor-plan execution wave step must be included in the flow, and Shipment Labor Planning Criteria determine which shipments contribute for a labor group.
claims.limits: Estimated labor is separate from actual labor activity. The source gives no universal estimate, accurate deployment standard or complete service-to-database mapping.

claims.statement: The labor-report illustration is explicitly a custom example rather than an existing report, with SCI dependency. The later future-functionality note says labor configuration/time values still need review and SCI reports need development. The performance-management page contains headings for reporting, event management and historical analysis without populated requirements.
claims.limits: An empty requirements section and a sample chart are not report acceptance, verified timing or evidence that no reporting requirement exists.

claims.statement: VAS and base Inbound QC are listed as future test candidates, with document updates and additional scope needed if adopted. Their inclusion in future-functionality pages does not establish use in the described migration.
claims.limits: Prospective implementation choices only; neither test completion nor implementation acceptance is documented here.

claims.limits: The document title and unsigned form do not establish customer approval, a deployed system or present owner acceptance.

diagrams.title: Outbound process and actor distinction
diagrams.description: A left-to-right flow shows Shipment Creation, Wave Processing, Picking, Packing, Staging and Shipping. Rectangles denote processes normally done by the system; trapezoids denote those normally requiring user interaction. Labels describe reserving stock, retrieving inventory, identifying box contents, staging and confirming departure.
diagrams.limits: High-level typical flow, not an exhaustive dependency graph. It does not make every step automatic or establish this deployment.
